import pandas as pd
from datetime import timedelta

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    target_snapshot = inputs["target_snapshot"].copy()
    cdc_events = inputs["cdc_events"].copy()
    watermark = inputs["watermark"].copy()
    
    # Extract the high_ts watermark value
    high_ts = watermark["high_ts"].iloc[0]
    
    # Filter events that are strictly after the watermark
    new_events = cdc_events[cdc_events["event_ts"] > high_ts].copy()
    
    # Sort events by user_id, event_ts, event_seq for sequential processing
    new_events = new_events.sort_values(by=["user_id", "event_ts", "event_seq"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Initialize result as a copy of target_snapshot
    result = target_snapshot.copy()
    
    # Convert result to dict for easier updates keyed by user_id
    result_dict = {}
    for _, row in result.iterrows():
        user_id = row["user_id"]
        result_dict[user_id] = {
            "user_id": row["user_id"],
            "email": row["email"],
            "status": row["status"],
            "status_ts": row["status_ts"]
        }
    
    # Process each event sequentially
    for _, event in new_events.iterrows():
        user_id = event["user_id"]
        event_ts = event["event_ts"]
        op = event["op"]
        email = event["email"]
        
        # Get current state for this user (or initialize if not exists)
        if user_id not in result_dict:
            current_state = {
                "user_id": user_id,
                "email": None,
                "status": None,
                "status_ts": None
            }
        else:
            current_state = result_dict[user_id].copy()
        
        if op == "D":
            # Soft delete: mark as DELETED, preserve email, update status_ts
            current_state["status"] = "DELETED"
            current_state["status_ts"] = event_ts
            # email stays as is
        
        elif op == "U":
            # Update operation
            if current_state["status"] is None or current_state["status"] == "ACTIVE":
                # User is new or currently ACTIVE: apply the update
                current_state["email"] = email
                current_state["status"] = "ACTIVE"
                current_state["status_ts"] = event_ts
            
            elif current_state["status"] == "DELETED":
                # User is DELETED: check resurrection window
                # Resurrection is allowed only if event_ts is STRICTLY MORE than 7 days after status_ts
                deletion_ts = current_state["status_ts"]
                resurrection_threshold = deletion_ts + timedelta(days=7)
                
                if event_ts > resurrection_threshold:
                    # Resurrection is allowed
                    current_state["email"] = email
                    current_state["status"] = "ACTIVE"
                    current_state["status_ts"] = event_ts
                # else: update is discarded (deletion is sticky)
        
        result_dict[user_id] = current_state
    
    # Convert result_dict back to DataFrame
    result_rows = list(result_dict.values())
    new_snapshot = pd.DataFrame(result_rows)
    
    # Ensure correct column order and types
    new_snapshot = new_snapshot[["user_id", "email", "status", "status_ts"]]
    new_snapshot["user_id"] = new_snapshot["user_id"].astype("int64")
    new_snapshot["email"] = new_snapshot["email"].astype("object")
    new_snapshot["status"] = new_snapshot["status"].astype("object")
    new_snapshot["status_ts"] = new_snapshot["status_ts"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    
    return {"new_snapshot": new_snapshot}
